content: Do not take this medication in combination with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, metaxalone, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, or tranylcypromine. Additionally, most MAO inhibitors should not be taken for at least two weeks before starting this medication. Certain products may contain ingredients that can elevate your heart rate or blood pressure. Caffeine can amplify the side effects of this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Important Notes: Do not share this medication with others. Appetite suppressants should not be used as a substitute for a proper diet. Your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, heart function, kidney function) while you are taking this medication. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. How to Use This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually 1 to 3 times daily. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Your doctor will adjust the dose to determine the most effective amount for you. Use this medication regularly and exactly as prescribed to achieve the best results. Benzphetamine is typically prescribed for only a few weeks at a time. It should not be taken with other appetite suppressants (refer to the Drug Interactions section). If you suddenly stop using this medication, you may experience withdrawal symptoms such as depression or severe fatigue. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have used benzphetamine for a long time or in high doses. Addiction Risk: While this medication helps many people, it may sometimes cause addiction. The risk of addiction is higher if you have a history of substance use disorder (e.g., overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol). Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. This medication may become less effective over time. If this occurs, consult your doctor. Do not increase the dose unless directed by your doctor. Side Effects: Common side effects include dizziness, dry mouth, difficulty sleeping, irritability, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. This medication may raise your blood pressure. Rarely, it can cause serious (sometimes fatal) lung or heart problems, such as pulmonary hypertension or heart valve issues. The risk increases with prolonged use of this medication and concurrent use of other appetite-suppressant drugs or herbal products. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking benzphetamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other sympathomimetic amines (e.g., decongestants like pseudoephedrine, stimulants like amphetamine, appetite suppressants like phentermine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Benzphetamine must not be used during pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Infants born to mothers who have used this medication for a prolonged period or in high doses may experience withdrawal symptoms such as irritability or extreme fatigue. This drug may pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Taking MAO inhibitors with this medication may cause a serious (possibly fatal) drug interaction. Avoid taking MAO inhibitors (e.g., isocarboxazid, linezolid, metaxalone, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, tranylcypromine) during treatment with this medication. Most MAO inhibitors should also not be taken for two weeks before starting this medication. Some products contain ingredients that may raise your heart rate or blood pressure. Caffeine can increase the side effects of this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Do not share this medication with others.
